table_title: List major philosophical schools across world traditions, with their founding figure, approximate founding period, and origin region.
db_analog: SELECT s.school_name AS school, s.founding_figure, s.founding_period_approximate, s.origin_region FROM philosophical_schools s WHERE s.school_id IN (curator_screened_school_ids) ORDER BY s.approximate_founding_century_anchor ASC, s.school_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of philosophies' master article (universe-discovery only) + 23 per-school Wikipedia articles, master accessed 2026-05-15; the 23 per-school articles re-grounded 2026-06-02 during the approved scope rebuild. Universe = 23 curator-screened major philosophical schools (claim_type = `candidate_rebuild`). The master 'List of philosophies' is a broad cross-tradition enumeration that does NOT itself cleanly anchor a Greek + Indian + Chinese + Medieval + Modern slate with founding-figure/period/origin triples, so the universe is rebuilt across the master + per-school articles. The 2026-06-02 rebuild replaced the prior strict 'single originating founder, foregrounded in the school's own article lede' admission rule (which had been applied inconsistently — it admitted Yoga / Mimamsa / Nyaya, which are systematizer / sutra-author / traditional-attribution cases, while excluding Advaita Vedanta / Samkhya / Charvaka for the very same reason) with an INCLUSIVE, uniformly-applied rule: a major philosophical school that has a single conventionally-associated FOUNDING FIGURE — an originator, a systematizer, or a traditionally-attributed founder. Schools with no single associated figure are excluded (Legalism: Shang Yang / Shen Buhai / Shen Dao / Han Fei — the article presents multiple strands, not one figure). temporal_sensitivity = low because the underlying historical facts are stable historiographically; several founding-figure attributions are genuinely disputed or legendary (Laozi, Kapila, Brihaspati, Mahavira-as-24th-tirthankara/reviver, Adi-Shankara-as-systematizer) and are documented in curation.json as expected low-confidence calibration cells, not errors. Per-row Approximate Founding Period is a TEXT categorical (NOT numeric year) accepting article phrasing like 'c. 5th century BCE', 'c. 6th–5th century BCE', 'c. 1st millennium BCE', 'c. 8th century CE', 'c. early 20th century CE' — numeric year would create artificial precision against sources that use centuries/ranges. Per-row Origin Region is a curator-normalized region grounded in the school's own Wikipedia article (lede where present, otherwise a documented body/category locator, otherwise the foregrounded founding figure's documented national/regional context); see curation.json normalization_decisions for the per-cell locators. Buddhism Origin Region was corrected from the unsupported 'Northern India' to the lede-grounded 'eastern Gangetic plain' (Buddhism lede: 'It arose in the eastern Gangetic plain ... in the 5th century BCE'). Column renamed Founder -> Founding Figure to make the inclusive scope (originator / systematizer / traditional attribution) honest. **Canonical Text column was considered and DROPPED** at the original design pass: screening found only ~68% of candidate schools had a single foregrounded canonical text (below the 70% threshold), so the column would have forced curator scalarization.
_extraction_notes: Qualitative instance — single-source-per-row attribute projection over a curator-screened entity set (operation_type = projection; the structural primitive is a multi-column SELECT over a curator-screened school set, NOT a two-table join). Source universe = 23 curator-screened philosophical schools assembled across Wikipedia's broad 'List of philosophies' master (universe-discovery only) + 23 per-school articles (each grounding one row's Founding Figure + Approximate Founding Period + Origin Region). APPROVED SCOPE REBUILD (2026-06-02): the prior 18-row universe used a strict 'single originating founder foregrounded in the school's own article lede' admission rule that was applied INCONSISTENTLY (it admitted Yoga/Mimamsa/Nyaya, which are systematizer/sutra-author/traditional-attribution cases, while excluding Advaita Vedanta/Samkhya/Charvaka for the identical reason). It was replaced with an INCLUSIVE, uniformly-applied rule that matches the natural query 'major philosophical schools and their founders': a major school that has a single conventionally-associated FOUNDING FIGURE (originator, systematizer, OR traditionally-attributed founder). Under the inclusive rule: KEEP all 18 prior rows; ADD 5 (Daoism->Laozi, Advaita Vedanta->Adi Shankara, Samkhya->Kapila, Jainism->Mahavira, Charvaka->Brihaspati); EXCLUDE Legalism (no single conventionally-associated figure — Shang Yang/Shen Buhai/Shen Dao/Han Fei; the article presents multiple strands). The `Founder` column was renamed `Founding Figure` everywhere to make the inclusive scope honest (an originator/systematizer/traditional attribution is a 'founding figure', not necessarily 'the founder'). Schema: 4 cols (School PK + Founding Figure categorical + Approximate Founding Period categorical-text + Origin Region categorical). Sort: regularized to a single consistent rule when the 5 rows were added — primary = earliest-century anchor of the founding period (oldest first; BCE before CE), minor tiebreak = range-end / 'late' modifier (later sorts after), final tiebreak = School ASC. (The prior order had minor internal inconsistencies, e.g., Buddhism before Confucianism; the regularized key is documented in curation.json decision_log.) Tradition distribution after rebuild: Indian 9 (Charvaka, Samkhya, Jainism, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Buddhism, Mimamsa, Yoga, Advaita Vedanta), Chinese 3 (Confucianism, Daoism, Mohism), Hellenistic 6 (Aristotelianism, Platonism, Pyrrhonism, Epicureanism, Stoicism, Neoplatonism), Medieval 3 (Avicennism, Thomism, Scotism), Modern Western 2 (Cartesianism, Phenomenology) = 23. Founding Figure column: 23 distinct values. Approximate Founding Period: TEXT format accepting article ranges. Origin Region: redefined as curator-normalized region grounded in the school's own article (lede where present, else a documented body/category locator, else the foregrounded founding figure's documented national/regional context) — per-cell locators are in curation.json. Buddhism Origin Region corrected from the unsupported 'Northern India' to the lede-grounded 'eastern Gangetic plain'. Several founding-figure cells are genuinely disputed/legendary (Laozi, Kapila, Brihaspati, Mahavira, Adi Shankara) and are documented in curation.json as expected low-confidence calibration cells. claim_type = `candidate_rebuild` (the universe membership is curator-judgment per the inclusive admission rule; the master list does not source-define the slate). operation_type changed from `join` (invalid for query_category=qualitative under the local validate_operation_query_pair, which allows only {filter, projection}) to `projection`. source_count = 28 (1 master universe-discovery URL + 23 per-school value/entity-detail URLs + 4 founder-context origin-grounding URLs; source_count == len(source_urls)). Entity class: `abstract-categories/philosophical-schools`. REPAIR cycle 4 (addresses codex cycle-3 re-audit, 2 BLOCKING): (1) added 4 founder biography pages (Husserl, Aquinas, Duns Scotus, Descartes) to source_urls so the 4 founder-context Origin Region cells (Phenomenology=Germany, Thomism=Italy/France, Scotism=Scotland/Paris, Cartesianism=France) are grounded in a CITED source rather than uncited founder-context; source_count 24->28. (2) Period cells revised to source-faithful ranges: Nyaya 'c. 6th century BCE' -> 'c. 6th century BCE–2nd century CE'; Mimamsa 'c. 3rd century BCE' -> 'c. 3rd–2nd century BCE'; Yoga 'c. 2nd century BCE' -> 'c. first half of the 1st millennium CE' (the article gives no 2nd-c-BCE founding for the school; Yoga Sutras circulated in the first half of the 1st millennium CE). CSV row order unchanged (sort anchors did not move).
